name: jq
summary: A portable JSON processor that evaluates composable filters over JSON value streams and exposes the results through a command-line input, output, and status interface.

features.name: Composable filter language
features.description: The jq manual models a program as a filter with an input and output, and documents composition operators that feed one filter's outputs into another filter or concatenate multiple result streams.
benefits: Makes extraction, transformation, and aggregation reusable as small expressions
Supports composition without requiring a separate host-language program
costs: Filter evaluation semantics must be understood to predict cardinality and ordering
Complex expressions can become a separate language-maintenance surface

features.name: JSON value stream processing
features.description: The official manual describes JSON entities as an input stream processed one at a time, with filters able to produce zero, one, or multiple output values; it also documents a streaming parser mode for large inputs.
benefits: Allows pipeline-style processing of successive JSON values
Provides a streaming mode that can avoid materializing a complete input tree
costs: Streaming changes the representation to path/value events that consumers must interpret
Filters that require whole-input context may need slurping and more memory

features.name: Portable command-line boundary
features.description: The upstream README describes jq as portable C with zero runtime dependencies, while the manual defines a command-line filter argument, file or standard-input inputs, standard-output results, and documented exit statuses.
benefits: Fits shell pipelines and automation with a small process boundary
Reduces runtime deployment dependencies for the standalone processor
costs: Textual command invocation and JSON output remain outside typed host-language contracts
Portability still leaves platform, locale, and filesystem behavior as external concerns

mathematical_views.question: How does a jq filter transform one input value stream into an ordered output value stream?
assumptions: A filter is modeled as a relation or transducer that may emit zero or more values for each input
The view abstracts parser buffering, memory management, and command-line option handling
Stream ordering is treated as observable while external side effects are excluded from the model

mathematical_views.question: Which composition operators preserve a useful stream interface when filters are chained or branched?
assumptions: Filter composition is modeled by feeding outputs forward and concatenating branch outputs
The model abstracts errors, resource limits, and filters with external effects
The view describes candidate algebraic structure rather than proving equivalence of arbitrary programs

benefits: Small expressions compose into reusable transformations
costs: Cardinality and evaluation behavior add language-specific reasoning cost

benefits: Supports both per-value pipelines and explicit whole-input aggregation
costs: Consumers trade memory savings for streaming-specific path/value handling

benefits: Simple portable integration point for scripts and tools
costs: Process and textual interfaces provide less structure than an embedded API
